issue: ਭਗਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੈ ਮਨਿ ਬਿਸ੍ਰਾਮ: does the Naam rest (abide) in the devotees' minds, or do the devotees' minds find rest in it? Also: the marker ਰਹਾਉ is left out of the English, like a verse number.
our reading: Sukhmani, the jewel of peace, is God's Naam, the nectar of peace; it rests in the minds of the devotees. (No 'Pause'.)
alternatives: '… in it the minds of the devotees find rest' (our Hindi gives both; Sant Singh Khalsa: the minds of the devotees abide in peace). If the exporter does not add ਰਹਾਉ, end with 'Pause.'

issue: ਬੇਦ ਪੁਰਾਨ ਸਿੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਿ ਸੁਧਾਖੵਰ ॥ ਕੀਨੇ ਰਾਮ ਨਾਮ ਇਕ ਆਖੵਰ: were the scriptures made from the one word of the Name, or did the scriptures declare that one word the purest of words?
our reading: The Vedas, the Puranas and the Simritis, pure words all, were made from the one word of the Lord's Name (as our Hindi).
alternatives: The Vedas, Puranas and Simritis have made (declared) the one word of the Lord's Name the purest of words.

issue: ਪ੍ਰਭ ਕੈ ਸਿਮਰਨਿ ਹੋਇ ਸੁ ਭਲਾ
our reading: whatever happens is good (as our Hindi)
alternatives: one becomes good (Sant Singh Khalsa); whatever happens seems good to one

issue: ਪ੍ਰਭ ਕਉ ਸਿਮਰਹਿ ਸਦਾ ਅਬਿਨਾਸੀ has no ਸੇ, so ਸਦਾ ਅਬਿਨਾਸੀ could describe God.
our reading: All who remember God become forever imperishable (as our Hindi).

issue: ਹਰਿ ਸਿਮਰਨਿ ਧਾਰੀ ਸਭ ਧਰਨਾ and ਹਰਿ ਸਿਮਰਨਿ ਕੀਓ ਸਗਲ ਅਕਾਰਾ: our Hindi reads 'for the sake of Simran' (के लिये), but ਸਿਮਰਨਿ is instrumental/locative (by, through, in). Also ਹਰਿ ਸਿਮਰਨਿ ਲਗਿ ਬੇਦ ਉਪਾਏ has no subject; 'the sages' is supplied.
our reading: Through Simran of the Lord the whole earth is upheld; through Simran of the Lord all visible creation was made; absorbed in Simran of the Lord, the sages brought forth the Vedas.
alternatives: For the sake of Simran the earth was established and creation made (our Hindi, Sant Singh Khalsa); 'the Vedas were composed' without naming who.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਕੇ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਸਾਥ: a prayer (be with Nanak) or a vocative (O God, Nanak's companion)?
our reading: I have come to your refuge; O God, stay with Nanak (as our Hindi).
alternatives: O God, ever with Nanak, I have come to your refuge.

issue: ਲਾਖ ਕਰੋਰੀ ਬੰਧੁ ਨ ਪਰੈ: object of ਬੰਧੁ is implied.
our reading: Gathering hundreds of thousands and millions, one sets no bound to craving (as our Hindi).
alternatives: One with lakhs and crores is not freed of bondage (ਬੰਧੁ as bond).

issue: Our Hindi renders ਅਸ੍ਵ ਹੈਵਰ as घोड़े, हाथी; ਹੈਵਰ (Skt. hayavara) is the finest horse, elephants being ਗੈਵਰ (gajavara). Our glossary already has 'fine horses, steeds'.
our reading: gold, horses, the finest steeds and land
alternatives: gold, horses, elephants and land (our Hindi, Sant Singh Khalsa)

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਬੋਲੈ ਸਹਜਿ ਸੁਭਾਇ: ਬੋਲੈ is third person singular; our Hindi has an imperative (बोलो).
our reading: Nanak utters it in natural poise and with love.
alternatives: Speak it with natural ease (our Hindi, Sant Singh Khalsa); whoever utters it in poise and love (is freed of pain).

issue: ਬਿਖੋਟਿ is uncommon: what is lost?
our reading: he throws away his good faith (his trust and credit), as our Hindi

issue: ਜੋ ਤੁਮ ਭਾਨੇ ਤਿਨ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਜਾਤਾ: ਪ੍ਰਭੁ is nominative/accusative, not vocative; our Hindi has 'तुम्हें जाना'.
our reading: Those who please you have known God.
alternatives: Those who please you, O God, have known you.

issue: ਕਰਉ ਬੇਨਤੀ: ਕਰਉ is first person singular; our Hindi has an imperative (विनती करो).
our reading: I offer my prayer to the Supreme Lord, who knows everything.
alternatives: Offer your prayer to the Supreme Lord, who knows everything (our Hindi, Sant Singh Khalsa).

issue: Is ਬਿਨਸਿ ਜਾਇ a wish, or a statement that the vices perish in God's refuge?
our reading: May lust, anger, greed, attachment and egotism be destroyed. Nanak seeks the refuge of God: O divine Guru, grant your grace (as our Hindi).
alternatives: In God's refuge lust, anger, greed, attachment and egotism are destroyed; O divine Guru, grant your grace (that Nanak may reach it).

issue: ਗੁਰ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਜਸੁ ਕਹੈ: ਕਹੈ is third person singular; our Hindi has an imperative (कह).
our reading: by the Guru's grace Nanak speaks his praise
alternatives: by the Guru's grace, speak his praise (our Hindi, Sant Singh Khalsa); by the Guru's grace one speaks his praise

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਜਾਪੁ ਜਪੈ ਜਪੁ ਸੋਇ: grammar of the cognate repetition is loose.
our reading: says Nanak, repeat his Name, and his alone (ਸੋਇ = that very one)
alternatives: Nanak repeats that very chant; meditate and chant his chant (Sant Singh Khalsa)

issue: ਮਃ ੫ is rendered 'the Fifth Guru'; our Hindi also names Guru Arjan Dev Ji.
our reading: Sukhmani, in Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru.
alternatives: … by the Fifth Guru, Guru Arjan Dev Ji; or keep 'Mehla 5'.
